newsitem.title: USA: Everest Medical goal is profit in '97.
newsitem.headline: Everest Medical goal is profit in '97.

text.p: Everest Medical Corp president John Shannon Jr said achieving profitability in 1997 is among the medical device manufacturer's goals for 1997.
"Among the company's goals is "achievement of profitability for the year," Shannon said in a statement.
Shannon also said Everest seeks to increase its share in the core business of laparoscopy and to create a market presence in minimally-invasive cardiac surgery.

"We continue to invest prudently in the future. We are convinced that bi-polar electrosurgery has the potential to become the standard of care for the new minimally invasive cardiac surgery marketplace," Shannon said.

Everest said Monday it narrowed its losses in the fourth quarter and for the full year. For the quarter, it posted a loss of $0.01 a share compared to a year-ago loss of $0.04. For all of 1996, it lost $0.11 a share compared to a loss of $0.18 a share in 1995. Share results reflect payment of preferred dividends.
Full-year revenues rose to $6.0 million from $4.3 million.
"The substantial improvement in gross margin coupled with prudent management of operating expenses has resulted in a significant movement towards profitability," Shannon noted.
